name: Northern Mali pearl millet with domestication traits
description: Pearl millet chaff preserved in pottery from northern Mali shows changes associated with domestication, including non-shattering plant structures and increased grain size.

impact.note: Chaff in pottery from one area showing pearl millet being domesticated; a new ability locally, on the line to millet farming across Africa.

date.label: Approximately 3020–1940 calibrated BCE
date.basis: The source reports a 3020–1940 cal BCE date on organic material in an MK36 potsherd; its authors consider a middle-to-late third millennium date likely and caution about old carbon.

events.statement: Pearl millet chaff preserved in pottery from northern Mali shows changes associated with domestication, including non-shattering plant structures and increased grain size.
events.caveats: The dated sherd and the assemblage are not necessarily contemporaneous; the organic date may be affected by old carbon. The proposed later third-millennium chronology is an interpretation, not a hard bound on every sherd.

evidence.locator: Materials and Methods, p. 215; Results and discussion, pp. 220–222
evidence.supports: MK36 organic material dated 3020–1940 cal BCE; the authors infer a later third-millennium assemblage containing both wild and domestication-type traits, and compare estimated grain breadth across sites.

earliest_record.rationale: The date represents the cited MK36 pottery-material age estimate; the source favours a later third-millennium interpretation but the calibration range reaches into the second millennium BCE. The date does not establish the start of domestication.

caveats: The dated sherd and the assemblage are not necessarily contemporaneous; the organic date may be affected by old carbon. The proposed later third-millennium chronology is an interpretation, not a hard bound on every sherd.

research.note: Independent check of the cited passages and marked facets on 2026-11-09; interpretations and date limits retain the stated caveats.
